topics.label: Welcome and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course context, outlines the learning objectives, and frames the central question of what causes cancer.

topics.label: Genetic, endogenous, and environmental contributions to cancer etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer arises from an interplay between endogenous mutations, microenvironmental factors, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Biological, physical, and chemical carcinogens and their mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific causative agents—including viruses, dietary toxins, UV radiation, and metabolically activated chemicals—and the molecular mechanisms by which they induce DNA alterations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and life-stage susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic aspects of carcinogenesis, focusing on the two-stage initiation-promotion model, inflammatory microenvironments, and tissue susceptibility during specific developmental stages.

topics.label: Methods for detecting mutational signatures and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate human cancer risk.
